cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. These are the sons of Jacob, also called Israel, who went down to Egypt with their father: Reuben, Judah, Benjamin and the rest, each one bringing his whole family. Count everybody up, plus Jacob's son Joseph, who was already in Egypt, and Jacob's descendants come to seventy.
Then Joseph dies. All his brothers die, and that whole generation is gone.

cards.question: Joseph and his whole generation are gone. What happens to the Israelites in Egypt now?

answers.text: They multiply until the land is filled with them
They dwindle down to just a few families
They pack up and head back to Canaan

cards.text: Then a new king comes to power in Egypt, one who did not know Joseph. Picture a brand new manager who's never heard of ANYBODY, except this one runs a whole COUNTRY.

cards.question: The new king tells his people the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for them. If a war breaks out, what is he afraid the Israelites will do?

answers.text: Join Egypt's enemies and fight against Egypt
Hide out in the hills until the war ends
Refuse to send Egypt a single soldier

cards.question: The king's plan is to deal shrewdly with the Israelites before they increase even more.
The Egyptians appointed ___ over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor.
All that forced labor builds two store cities for Pharaoh. Which ones?
The more the Egyptians oppress the Israelites, the fewer Israelites there are.
The Israelites keep multiplying and flourishing no matter what Egypt does. How do the Egyptians come to feel about them?

cards.text: You'd think somebody in Pharaoh's court would raise a hand and go, "Uh, maybe the plan isn't working?" Nope. They work the Israelites ruthlessly.

cards.question: The Egyptians made the Israelites' lives bitter with hard labor in ___ and ___, and with all kinds of work in the fields.

cards.text: Then the king of Egypt calls in two Hebrew midwives. Their names are Shiphrah and Puah.

cards.question: The king tells Shiphrah and Puah to watch the Hebrew women on the birthstools. What is his order?

answers.text: Kill the sons but let the daughters live
Bring every son straight to the palace
Send every son off to the taskmasters

cards.question: Shiphrah and Puah do as the king of Egypt instructed.
The midwives let the Hebrew boys live. What's behind it?

cards.text: So the king of Egypt summons the midwives, and friend, you know that stomach drop when your boss says "Got a minute?" Now make the boss PHARAOH.

cards.question: The king asks, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?” The midwives tell Pharaoh the Hebrew women give birth before a midwife arrives.
So God was ___ to the midwives, and the people ___ and became even more numerous.
Because the midwives feared God, what does He give them?

cards.text: But Pharaoh isn't done. This time he skips the midwives and gives the order to all his people.

cards.question: Pharaoh gives all his people an order about every son born to the Hebrews. What must they do?

answers.text: Hand him over to the army

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Hang onto your apron, friend, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: In Exodus 1:8 the new king did not know Joseph. The joke changes that to a manager who has never heard of ANYBODY, so the comparison no longer has the same action. It also mixes the manager image with the Bible setting ('except this one runs a whole COUNTRY'). The joke would land better as a new boss who has never heard of the one person everybody owes.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The second sentence puts the manager comparison and the king of Egypt into one image instead of keeping them separate.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card cites Exodus 1:9-10, but the right answer ('Join Egypt's enemies and fight against Egypt') comes only from Exodus 1:10. Verse 9 is only setup in the question.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line opens with 'And that's where we'll leave it for now.' That is copied word for word from the doc's example instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage, but it cites Exodus 1:22. Verse 22 was already told on card 9 and asked on card 10. The rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, no wider. This card tells no verses, yet the output format requires a verses field.
findings.question: When a last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field be: the passage's last verse, empty or null, or something else?
